proposals.evidence: Turner kīdṛśa explicitly gives Old Marwari kiso, Hindi kaisā, Punjabi kihā/kihṛā, Marathi kasā and related kis-/kas-/keh- type interrogatives. These survey forms fit that what-kind family, including local inflection and extensions. The extended -l-/-n- forms are qualified regional comparisons, not independent reconstructions of each suffix.

proposals.evidence: Turner kīdṛśa explicitly derives Gujarati śũ what through *ksiũ with loss of the vowel. These neighbouring Bhili/Bareli/Gojri hū̃/sū forms are compared with that Gujarati-area interrogative, with local s/h alternation and loss of written nasalization retained. The exact regional contact route remains open.
